transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... the thought of getting on an airplane right now just scares me so bad. I mean, I know it doesn't make sense logically, but my body just reacts. It's like it just tells me that the plane is going to fall. It's gotten really hard to deal with, so I figured I needed to see someone about it.
Is it just airplanes that trigger this fear, or are there other situations that cause you to feel similarly anxious?

No, it's really just airplanes. I mean, I don't have a problem with heights or enclosed spaces or anything like that. I can ride in elevators, I can go to the top of tall buildings, none of that bothers me. It's specifically just flying. The whole process of being on a plane.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of flying?

It's been about seven months now. It all started right after I lost my job at the clinic. I took a flight on this small plane, and... well, it was incredibly turbulent. Just a really rough ride. And ever since that specific flight, this fear has just been there.
Has this fear of flying been affecting your daily life or causing you significant distress beyond just the act of flying itself?

Yeah, it really has. I mean, as a physician, I sometimes need to travel for work. I've had to turn down coverage that requires flying, which... well, it's cost me income. And it's starting to make my colleagues question if they can actually rely on me. I've also had to skip out on some important professional meetings. And on a personal level, I've been putting off seeing my family because I just can't bring myself to get on a plane to visit them.
Does thinking about flying, even when you're not actually at an airport or on a plane, trigger this fear response in you?

Yeah, it definitely does. Just... even if I just get an email about a rural shift that requires a flight, my heart starts pounding right away. My hands get all sweaty, and I feel like I literally can't breathe until I just close the message and look away. It's immediate.
Do you experience this fear response when you see pictures or videos of airplanes, aside from just thinking about flying?

No, not really. If I just see a picture of a plane, or watch a video of one on TV, that doesn't bother me. It's really just tied to the actual prospect of me having to get on one. So, no, just looking at them doesn't cause that reaction.
Do you actively avoid flying whenever possible because of this fear?

Yes, absolutely. Like I was saying earlier, I've canceled clinic coverage and skipped medical meetings because of it. I've also put off seeing my family down in Honduras. I just avoid it completely because I cannot make myself go to the airport. The only way I can even endure it is if I am shaking and holding on to someone the whole time. So, yeah, I avoid it whenever I possibly can.
Has your fear of flying affected your relationships with friends or family in any way?

Yes, it has. I mean, like I mentioned, I've delayed seeing my family in Honduras, which has been hard on us. But it's also really affecting my professional relationships. Because I keep turning down that flight-based clinic coverage, it's actually cost me income, and my colleagues are starting to question whether they can even rely on me. I've also had to miss some really important professional meetings because I just can't get on a plane. So, yeah, it's definitely taking a toll on a lot of things.
Are there any other areas of your life, besides work and visiting family, where this fear of flying is causing problems for you?

Not really, no. I mean, work and family are the main things. I guess I don't really take vacations that require flying either, but the main problems are just missing out on seeing my family and the issues it's causing at work. That's pretty much it.
Are you avoiding any social events or hobbies that you would normally enjoy because of your fear of flying?

No, not really. I mean, most of my hobbies and the social stuff I do are just around town. So it doesn't really get in the way of that. It's really just the traveling part—work and family—like I said.
